Results.ReviewText: First time purchasing a Weber. Used it a few times and am very pleased. Sear zone works really well. Good small format grill. Like the three burner vs. two burner that are usually standard in grills of the same size.

Results.ReviewText: I am really liking my Spirit E-325 gas grill.  Fits perfectly on our deck with fold down side shelves that are usually unavailable with 3 burners out there.  Nice even cooking heat makes grilling easier.  The amount of cooking area allows for cooking with a griddle while charbroiling at the same time.  The searing option on 2 burners is a great feature also.  Webber’s longstanding quality and durability is what attracted me to the Webber grills to begin with.  It may cost a bit more, but in the long run, these grilling machines can’t be beat.  I am really looking forward to having a great summer barbecuing!
Results.Title: Check out the Spirit E-325

Results.ReviewText: This little grill is perfect for me.  I love to barbecue everything and it does a good job.  I love that the side trays can fold down.  The only thing I would add is a handle opposite side from the wheels to make it easier to push/pull into the position I want for grilling.  I would recommend this grill.

Results.ReviewText:
Nice grill perfect our small deck, Initially I was hesitant to get the "smaller" grill for when we had occasional guests etc but pretty much the entire surface is useable due to design so it has plenty of cooking space.
I had a gas grill years ago and had switched to a Weber charcoal grill which I liked but I missed the convenience of gas. I went with propane instead of natural gas so I could have more flexibility with the location. With natural gas it would have lived in one spot. 
I've used the seer function with both meat and veg and it works well. I can't tell you how it compares to an infrared grill but this one works great. I have 2 complaints. The Weber grill covers are overpriced and a previous one I had didn't last long and fell apart. I purchased an aftermarket brand that seems pretty good for 1/2 the price. My second complaint is industry-wide not just for Weber.... I don't like that the lid is flat on top so that basically water etc it's on top of it. Other than that so far so good. It doesn't have a lot of bells and whistles but I like it.

Results.ReviewText: in order to make a significant difference when using the "sear" feature, Weber seems to have under-powered the burners in their "normal" range.  With my last spirit, I was used to doing the bulk of my cooking using only one (of two) burners, full-on.  Now, i have to use two (of 3) and  keep making adjustments to keep in the temperature range I want.  I'm still ending up with a lot of underdone chicken and i'm hoping it's just a matter of getting used to the quirks of the grill.  I also find it difficult to tell if the igniter has actually lit the burner - usually takes two tries.  Overall - kind of a disappointing experience after years of having a dependable Weber gas grill.  But I have hope.

Results.ReviewText: A huge upgrade from our previous grill. My husband is a big fan. This is a mid-range gas grill that works great, durable, and user-friendly. It has reliable heat distribution, a spacious cooking area, and a sturdy build. I really like that there is a closed compartment for the propane tank to keep it out of sight. It has three burners with porcelain-enameled cast-iron cooking grates. It seems to withstand outdoor conditions well and resists rust. It does lack some of the high-tech additions of pricier models, but it more than makes up for it with excellent cooking performance and ease of use. My husband assembled the grill and said it was semi-difficult to put together. The hardest part was making sure everything was the right angle. So you might need some assistance during assembly.

Results.ReviewText:
This is our first Weber Grill. We have several friends who have them and without exception they rave about their grill’s high quality construction and performance. When our grill was ready for grill cemetery, we decided we wanted a Weber Grill.

One of the “must have” features for us was fold down sides. Because of where our grill is used and stored between uses, we wanted this feature. We also determined that a three-burner grill would best meet our needs both for cooking area, physical size and great grilling performance. With this in mind we searched on line and found that perfect Weber three-burner grill minus the fold-down sides. 

Nonetheless, we decided to go to Lowe’s and check out all grills in person. When we described our wish list to the salesman, we were thrilled that the new line of Weber Grills now included a three-burner model with fold down sides. After lifting the cover and turning the dials, the quality construction of the Weber Grill was obvious and we made the purchase.

After using the grill several times, we could not be happier with our decision. It cooks very evenly and offers great control over temperature. Preheating is fast and the searing feature is a bonus. 

If there is any learning curve, it would involve the lighting process.  You must read the manual to properly ignite the burners. On most grills, it is rather intuitive.  Not so on the Weber.  Pushing in on the knob, holding it in for 2 seconds, turning to the ignite position while continuing to push in and then continuing to push inward for an additional 2-5 seconds until the burner ignites.  Once mastered, not an issue.  But if a guest at your cookout offers to start your grill, tell them thanks but you’ll do it. 

I give this grill a 5-star rating without hesitation and highly recommend it. Quality and performance are excellent. I have never looked forward more to grilling, than I do now with this Weber Grill.
Results.Title: Three-burner Marvel
